summary.intent: Execute Phase 37 of the cipher-box project to implement a parallel batch upload pipeline, then clean up the code, add test coverage, and resolve PR review comments.
summary.outcome: Phase 37 completed with 2 plans: an SDK `uploadFiles()` batch method (Wave 1) and a Web Worker encryption offload + `useDropUpload` rewire (Wave 2). PR #416 created, code simplified, integration/E2E tests added, lint fixed, and 3 real bugs found in PR review were patched.

repo: The encrypt worker follows the same pattern as the existing `decrypt-sw.ts` service worker but needs its own entry in `tsconfig.sw.json` for CI type-checking coverage.
Vite handles `new Worker(new URL(..., import.meta.url))` natively — no extra config needed for dev/CI/prod worker builds.
`@cipherbox/crypto` uses Web Crypto API only (no Node.js crypto), making it safe to use inside Web Workers.

The codebase uses `ExternalEncryptFn` from `@cipherbox/sdk-core` as the canonical encryption function type — new code should reuse it via `ReturnType<>` / `Parameters<>` rather than redeclaring inline.
The project treats lint warnings as errors — `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` warnings in test files must be fixed, not ignored.
Task-reference comments like `(D-01)` are considered noise and should be removed; only non-obvious WHY comments are acceptable.
Blob `.buffer` usage in `upload.service.ts` violates `apps/web/CLAUDE.md` guidance — pre-existing debt to fix separately.

code.finding: Real bug: `params.data.length` becomes 0 after Transferable ArrayBuffer transfer. The byteLength must be captured before transfer.
`addFilePointerToFolder` collision error during batch upload should not abort the entire batch — it should be caught and the file demoted to a partial success, not thrown.
If `arrayBuffer()` or `uploadFiles()` throws inside the new-file batch path, upload rows get stuck in 'encrypting' state permanently. Needs a catch that marks all pending uploads as errored.

workflow: Worktree merges can silently fail if the branch ref isn't updated — cherry-picking specific commits from the worktree HEAD is a reliable fallback.
GSD verifier agents can produce false negatives if they run before cherry-picked commits are fully visible; always spot-check with Grep/file existence before accepting a `gaps_found` result.
Parallel executor agents commit with `--no-verify` to avoid hook contention; the orchestrator must run hooks once post-wave.
When running three parallel review agents (reuse, quality, efficiency), aggregating findings before acting avoids redundant fixes.
p-limit must be added as an explicit dependency after the SDK plan executes — it won't be auto-installed by pnpm workspaces.

friction: Wave 2 worktree branch ref wasn't updated after agent commits, requiring manual cherry-pick recovery.
The GSD verifier produced false negatives for all Wave 2 artifacts because it ran before cherry-picked commits were visible — required manual VERIFICATION.md correction.
Branch context confusion after cherry-picks: ended up in the worktree directory instead of the main repo, causing a bad merge that had to be reset.
PROJECT.md commit had to be retried after discovering the working directory had drifted to the wrong branch.
Stale worktree (`cipher-box-worktree-parallel`) left behind after execution and needed manual pruning during PR creation.
lint:fix run by user surfaced `any` type warnings that should have been caught before pushing — required a follow-up fix commit.
open_items: Web E2E tests not updated — existing upload Playwright tests cover single-file serial path only; multi-file batch drag-drop flows are untested in the browser.
Upfront file buffer allocation in `uploadFiles()` — all 3 review agents flagged memory concern for large batches; bounded by MAX_FILE_SIZE (100MB) for now but worth revisiting if batch sizes grow.
Blob `.buffer` usage in `apps/web/src/services/upload.service.ts` violates CLAUDE.md guidance — pre-existing issue, not addressed in this phase.
Cancel/abort support for batch uploads (AbortSignal passthrough in `uploadFiles()`) was flagged in PR review but deferred as out of scope.
Secondary pin warning not emitted in the batch path — identified in PR review, deprioritized.
